review.summary: T936 at 061d707f30bb610b908c807e5d00d8f6d0967913 preserves the old greedy ordering, stable ties, used-by-id behavior, and unchanged selectionValue/multiplier call order and count; non-finite values use the original sort comparator over identically ordered stored pairs. Scope is limited to declared touches and T936 itself. Independent checks passed: persisted-squads unit tests (29), the isolated automatic XI block (4, including its 300-run property), and 300 additional differential cases comparing exact Player identity and call traces across finite ties, shared IDs, NaN, infinities, undersized and empty squads. world.test.ts is classified as integration, so its new block was run explicitly with a name filter. Recorded world hashes exactly match 31243d16e32446febb0da343ce593a4fcb3fa042a474d9666017effdb36799c9 (1934) and 8dc13e17c9b093f7e5f6b1a943e586fa656b7907f5286b11a846cbc4efed873f (1950). All six A/B process runs report equal side output hashes across 12 timed pairs; independently recomputed CPU ratio is 0.9319 [0.8789, 0.9833]. Benchmark baseline differs from the assigned base only in spec documents; the measured implementation differs from the submitted commit only in T936 documentation. Submitted task-tier verification passed on the exact commit, including lint and i18n. Full integration, contract, build and batch remain coordinator gates.

reviewHistory.summary: T937 reviewed at 9165ceb2f220f9cd8934d73ea55c13ca3f44575f against original market base 79a417ccd and the current re-planned task on b68b0bffd. One P2 contract gap remains: Part 2 bypasses cache writes even though its unchanged acceptance requires the rejection to precede any cache write in the current walk. No behavioral regression was observed. Independent affected units passed: 3 files / 61 tests. An in-memory baseline/candidate comparison matched full worlds and exact NPC_WAGE_DECISIONS / PLAYER_MOVE_FLOW event traces in 54 tiny cases (252 events), including no books, wage excess, registration ceilings with reserved returns, available room, and equality at the wage limit. Part 1 preserves Slot and Player object identity, separate main OVR, fallback slots, Float64 precision, growth, and forget behavior; 1,288 additional cache reads matched the original map for zero, fractional, finite, NaN and infinite values on unchanged players and after forget. Source and tests match measured 49b7a5c2c. Saved world hashes match both required references; recomputed A/B statistics match all three artifacts, including combined CPU 0.8867 [0.8138, 0.9382], 12 pairs across 6 processes and equal hashes. Neither individual part claims a resolved gain. Submitted exact-commit verification passed typecheck, lint, format, i18n and 94 explicitly affected unit tests; broader host-load timing failures were not treated as passes. Long benchmarks, full suites and browser checks were not rerun; final integration, contract, build and batch remain coordinator gates.

findings.message: T937 explicitly permits Part 2 only when the original rejection precedes any observer call, draw or cache write in the current walk, and otherwise requires leaving Part 2 unchanged. That precondition is not met for a rejected buyer with a need and cold settlement caches: orderFor first writes the line/slot order and listing ratings (lines 465-482), and the registration/wage rejection in npcOffer also follows clubFacts storing its memo (line 146, reached through canRegister / npcOffer). The new break bypasses those writes, while refusesEveryListing itself can populate the buyer facts before rejecting it (line 267). The task result acknowledges the omitted memos, but the b68b0bffd re-plan changed the combined performance gate without allowing this exception. World hashes and differential tests support harmlessness for the checked cases; they do not satisfy the explicit no-cache-write precondition. Hand this gap to the planner to explicitly authorize bypassing proven equivalent settlement memo writes and document why delayed order construction cannot affect later decisions, or retain the original Part 2 walk and apply the task's combined-retention rule. Do not mark this acceptance complete under the current wording.

review.summary: T939 satisfies the re-planned recorded-experiment contract. Only handoff.mjs, handoff.json, text-handoff.patch and the task file differ from the assigned base; production code is unchanged. The script isolates synchronous sender serialization/postMessage time from receiver deserialization, using 15 alternating paired measurements per method. Recorded medians, intervals and 96.484375% order-statistic coverage recompute correctly: postMessage text/object is 1.303 [1.278, 1.318], so rejecting the change is supported. The archived patch applies to base and contains sensible checkpoint-equivalence, failure-response and queue-order units. Acceptance marks and result accurately report the negative outcome, proxy-only gate and Node/browser limitation. Submitted-commit task-tier records pass all five checks. Review ran only fast static, arithmetic, syntax and patch checks; no long benchmarks or suites.

T941 independently reviewed at 67a4a41367bf38c008942391f77683f79310d462 against its original base c9dfd49e7 and review base 6de16f223ced8e5c2d313022c50868eb912c4699. No actionable defects found. The key covers both shapes' tactic, roles, presence and freedom, side and slot count; production aggregatePlan constructs fixed formation roles without per-player presence/freedom, bounding ordinary play to 32 tables of at most 80 rows and 11 terms. Attribution/place overrides refresh and clear tables; lab attribution runs under withDefaultStaging, and probeLabReads explicitly refreshes before probing. Participation and skill exposure inputs are settled before SideLines is constructed, period and role IDs remain stable, and every weightsAt consumer reads its array. fitPlaceWeights is byte-identical to base. Independent units passed (4 files, 31 tests), and the requested placement integration passed (1 file, 5 tests). An in-memory base/candidate comparison matched complete player facts and traces in 60 cases covering warm caches, all tactics, repeated role/cell reads, slot changes, extra time, overrides and restoration; freezing candidate shared arrays produced no mutation errors. All 28,160 production place terms and five additional role/freedom/presence variants matched direct computation bit for bit. Recomputed every stored benchmark ratio and interval from raw pairs and verified hashes: final aggregate CPU 0.8096 [0.7981, 0.8240]; both retained parts independently improve CPU; part 3 was slower and restored. Day evidence is explicitly from the pre-restore candidate and remains contextual. Submission verification passed typecheck, lint, format, i18n, affected engine/lab units and aggregate integration; the authorized substitution for load-related unrelated timeouts is recorded. Final batch, contract and build gates remain with the coordinator. Changes stay within T941 scope.

review.summary: T938 at 83c0e7caaf0af738cb52f11b4c594dafb9098fab is approved. The per-line index exactly tracks cached settlementFacts.wanted, preserves club order through insertion and removal, and is refreshed after each destination-club facts recomputation, including across passes. Other clubs retain the same cached facts as before. Registration, affordability observers, offer ordering and signing operations remain unchanged; stature is deterministic from seed and club ID. The added regression compares events and the complete world with the reference implementation and covers newly wanted outfield signings on a later pass plus keeper-list removal. Reviewer-run free-agents and npc-careers units passed: 37/37. Runtime verification for the exact submitted commit records all five task checks passing, including 1360 affected unit tests. Stored generation hashes match the required 1934 and 1950 hashes, and the recorded source trees have identical production sources to the submission. Recomputed A/B statistics match the artifact: six processes, four pairs each, CPU ratio 0.9649 with 95% interval 0.9423-0.9967 and equal output hashes. The benchmark baseline is the attempt start commit 9bfd5e5ac; the later review-base lineup change is separate and presents no conflicting interaction. Changes stay within the authorized files. Final integration, contract and build verification remain with the coordinator.

T940 approved at 8a1cf5db91e653121b1aeda68154f597d51f8aff, comparing task changes against worker base 9bfd5e5ac and checking the group-base interaction. For valid fixture copies, ordered squad keys plus each complete squad JSON text preserve exactly the old squads serialization equality. The writer captures puts/drops/reorders before attribute-column filtering, while the shared context retains squads presence and all original non-squad inputs, including registry order. Snapshot, identity and reset behavior, reader/helper code, and the parity/registry comment remain intact. Changes stay within declared touches plus T940. Independent focused Vitest: 3 files, 36 tests passed; an in-memory baseline/candidate comparison passed 33 mutation/reset cases with identical patches and invalidation. Submitted task-tier verification records pass for this exact commit, including lint and i18n. The frozen benchmark writer/key match the worker base; 36 alternating paired samples across four rounds assert identical patches and rosterChanged. Saved timings reproduce median ratio 0.664 and interval [0.648, 0.719], with gains in both orders and every round. Despite reported host load and execution outside the heavy lock, this is acceptable evidence for the paired relative-performance claim. Integration, contract, build and final batch checks remain with the coordinator.
